paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. God has a job for every one of His people, and He is not vague about it. Three clans of Levites, three different loads: the holy objects, the curtains, the frames and posts. Nobody was left standing around asking, "So what do I do?" (Num 4:49)

It also teaches that God is holy, and He's serious about it. The Kohathites were told not to touch the holy objects, or they would die (Num 4:15), and not to go in and look, even for a moment (Num 4:20). But look at WHY He gave the order. He said it so they would "live and not die when they come near the most holy things" (Num 4:19). I think that's a God who sets a boundary because He wants His people to live.

So, baker, what do you take from it? Your place in God's work is not too small, because every load in that camp had a name on it, and every man was counted and given his work. Carrying curtains and tent pegs didn't look like much, but it was assigned by the LORD, and that is what made it matter. I know what it feels like to sit in the dark with nothing to do, so trust me: being handed a job by God is a gift.
